mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has turned up off its trough (-24.4 at t-2w to -21.9 at t-0w). This momentum reflects households progressively re-normalizing discretionary in-person trips, so the next 28-day mean sits above the last 28-day mean of about -23.2.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose 2.5 points from the t-2w trough to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is equal to or below the last 28-day mean, i.e. the t-0w uptick fails to extend past the t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has improved for two consecutive weeks (-31.9, -31.6, -30.3), signalling partial return of commuting routines. Recovered weekday presence feeds lunchtime and after-work retail footfall, lifting RETAIL_REC over the coming four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -31.9 at t-3w to -30.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES stays at or below -31 while RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean does not exceed the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has been pinned below -30 for the full four-week window with no net improvement (-33.3 to -32.9). Persistent transit suppression marks continuing capacity or restriction constraints that cap non-essential trip volumes, holding RETAIL_REC below its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean remains below -30 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT never exceeded -30.4 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT stays below -30 for the next two weeks yet RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean exceeds the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS spiked to +28.3 and remains volatile (+12.1 at t-0w). Elevated outdoor activity indicates leisure spending is being routed to free outdoor venues rather than indoor retail, so when PARKS exceeds +10 the retail series loses share and RETAIL_REC falls over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:weeks with PARKS above +10 (t-3w, t-0w) coincided with the two lowest RETAIL_REC improvements
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS exceeds +10, the following week's RETAIL_REC mean is at or above the preceding week's mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM sits near the pre-period baseline (-3.0 at t-0w) while other categories remain deeply negative. Near-baseline essential shopping shows in-person retail is tolerated, and as GROCERY_PHARM stabilises above -3.5 general retail footfall follows upward over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -3.6 at t-1w to -3.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rising above -3.0 is followed by a next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean at or below its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The mid-October seasonal cooling suppressed PARKS from +28.3 to +12.1 across the window. As outdoor alternatives become less attractive, leisure demand rotates back indoors and RETAIL_REC gains relative to its trailing four-week mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean declines more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 16.2 points between t-2w and t-1w as RETAIL_REC firmed
regime_hint: autumn cooling with declining outdoor season
failure_condition: A week-on-week PARKS decline of more than 5 points is followed by a lower RETAIL_REC weekly mean in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES identifies a suppressed-commuting state in which mobility curbs are binding. Jointly low readings on both series predict that discretionary retail visits keep shrinking, pushing RETAIL_REC below its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -30 and TRANSIT below -32 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:all four weeks show TRANSIT below -30 with WORKPLACES at or below -30.3
failure_condition: Weeks meeting the joint TRANSIT/WORKPLACES threshold are followed by a next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean above the last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has held at or above +6.7 for four straight weeks, showing a persistent at-home habit stock. Sustained home-stay keeps trip budgets compressed and caps retail recovery, so RETAIL_REC stays below its trailing mean over the next week unless RESIDENTIAL drops below +7.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean at or above +7 for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL logged 6.7, 7.7, 7.6 and 7.1 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: While RESIDENTIAL remains at or above +7, the next week's RETAIL_REC mean equals or exceeds the last 28-day mean.
